summary: Implement ADR-021: per-ticket lifecycle chain + async organizer checkpoint + verify-lifecycle
description:
Implement the ticket lifecycle trail integrity scheme decided in ADR-021 (TKT-57). Until this lands, `lifecycle_events` is append-only by policy (the `lifecycle_events_immutable` trigger, which is DDL and removable) and NOT tamper-evident — and ADR-003 §Decision 2 makes redemption decisions from that trace, so it is a fraud surface, not just an audit gap.

ADR-021 decides the WHAT; this ticket owns the HOW. Read ADR-021 in full before planning — every clause below is load-bearing and several are deliberate divergences from the money journal that must not be 'fixed' back.

Scope:
- Per-ticket hash chain (ticket-local sequence, previous_hash, entry_hash) in a COMPANION integrity table; `lifecycle_events` is immutable and must not be rewritten. Lifecycle row + integrity row in one transaction; verifiers assert one-to-one coverage.
- Appends serialize on the ticket row `Redeem` already locks (postgres.go:182). NO organizer-wide lock, ever — that constraint is the whole reason ADR-021 rejected copying the money journal.
- Asynchronous per-organizer checkpoint: signed Merkle root over per-ticket heads CHANGED since the previous checkpoint (delta, not full scan), chained to it. Default interval 60s.
- Ed25519 under an `access-lifecycle/` key namespace, distinct key material from `access-qr/` (token.go:61-78 has the keyring idiom).
- Sign the HEAD, not every entry (ADR-021 §Decision 5).
- `Redeem` fails OPEN with a high-severity alarm on a chain that does not verify (ADR-021 §Decision 6).
- `access verify-lifecycle` subcommand, public keys only; wire into `scripts/smoke.sh` against populated AND deliberately corrupted data, mirroring what smoke.sh:78-105 already does for `verify-journal`.
- Versioned, domain-separated canonical form; no PII, no `guest_order_ref`; pinned by golden tests.
- Resumable startup backfill, bounded and fail-fast per ADR-008; adopts existing history as baseline.
- Migrations: plain `CREATE INDEX`, never CONCURRENTLY (ADR-020 — migrations run at startup).

Test seam (verified to exist at HEAD): `services/access/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go` — already provisions an isolated PostgreSQL schema, upgrades 0001→0002, preserves issued/delivered history, redeems, and asserts the immutability trigger rejects an UPDATE. Extend it; next migration is 0003.

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
Spun out of **TKT-57**, which decided this ([ADR-021](../../docs/adr/ADR-021-ticket-lifecycle-trail-integrity.md)) and deliberately shipped decision-only. TKT-57 is closed by the ADR; this ticket is the one that actually closes the gap.

**Three things the TKT-57 plan gate flagged that this ticket inherits as obligations, not suggestions:**

1. **Checkpoint freshness must be monitored.** The async checkpoint is a job that can silently stop, and if it does, the trail degrades to per-ticket-only — reopening the exact fraud ADR-021 closes, *with no symptom at the gate*. A stale checkpoint is an integrity alarm. This is the single biggest risk in the design.
2. **The fail-open alarm must actually route somewhere.** ADR-021 §Decision 6 admits on a bad chain and alarms. That is only safe *because* the alarm is load-bearing — an unmonitored alarm turns the clause into a silent bypass. Own the routing, don't assume it.
3. **The checkpoint interval IS the fraud window.** A head rolled back before any checkpoint included it is undetectable. 60s is the default; justify it, don't inherit it.

**Two items from the TKT-57 draft are CONTESTED, not approved** — the Codex plan draft proposed them and the plan review pushed back. Justify them on their own merits here or drop them:

- Extracting a shared `services/access/internal/signing` package is **speculative until there is a second consumer**. Adding lifecycle key loading beside the QR loader in `cmd/access/main.go` may be the entire change.
- The `internal/ticket/token.go` refactor is scope this ticket must earn. The QR signer works; do not churn it to make the new code look symmetric.

**Also worth doing while here** (found during TKT-57 verification, not required by ADR-021): `scripts/smoke.sh:56` runs the access store smoke suite under `-run TestRedeemedLifecycleMigrationPreservesHistory`. That allowlist means a newly added smoke test silently never runs while the gate stays green. Lines 48 and 59 of the same file already call this out as a defect that stranded tests twice — access is the last block still carrying one. Drop the filter.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Amended after the TKT-57 Codex adversarial review (PR #49).** ADR-021 changed materially; three items below are now **prerequisites, not polish**. Re-read ADR-021 §Decision 2, §Decision 5 and §Decision 6 — the earlier draft of each overclaimed and was corrected.

1. **The checkpoint signer must refuse to launder a rollback.** It must not extend a chain whose head has regressed relative to the last root it observed — it must refuse and escalate. **That last-observed root has to live somewhere the database adversary does not control**, or the check is circular and buys nothing. Choosing where is this ticket's call and it is load-bearing: without it, an attacker truncates the checkpoint suffix and the signer re-blesses the rolled-back state under a fresh valid signature.

2. **Checkpoint freshness monitoring IS the detection mechanism** for targeted rollback — not a nice-to-have. ADR-021 §Decision 2 is explicit that the checkpoint does *not* make rollback cryptographically detectable; staleness is the only signal. Unmonitored, the checkpoint buys attacker cost and nothing else.

3. **Fail-open needs its bounds implemented, or it is a bypass.** ADR-021 §Decision 6 now mandates: **quarantine** (a ticket failing verification is admitted once, then every later scan is denied and escalated), **threshold escalation** (integrity failures above a configured rate flip the organizer into operator-controlled mode), and **alarm routing with response SLOs**. An unmonitored deployment must not run fail-open. Fail-open means a *crude* chain corruption also admits — the attacker needs no finesse.

4. **Epoch signatures at rotation.** Head-only signing means a compromised *current* key can rewrite a ticket's whole history. On each rotation the outgoing key signs the head as it stands and that signature is retained, so a later compromise cannot rewrite pre-rotation history. The head signature binds ticket identity, ticket-local sequence, canonical version and key id — **not the head hash alone**.

Everything in the original description still applies.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Amended again after the SECOND Codex adversarial pass (PR #49).** The first amendment above is now partly wrong — read this one instead where they disagree.

**The root cause, which supersedes the four separate items above:** every control I listed stores its state **in the Access database — the very database the adversary is defined as owning**. Quarantine rows, threshold counters, retained epoch signatures, the signer's last-observed root: all deletable or resettable by the same attacker who caused the failure. ADR-021 now leads with **§The trust boundary** saying exactly this. Do not add a control to this ticket whose evidence lives in Access and call it containment.

What that changes for this ticket:

1. **The checkpoint buys no detection today. It is scaffolding for TKT-11** — one anchorable root per interval instead of one per ticket head. Build it for that reason. Do not describe it in code comments, dashboards or metrics as rollback protection.
2. **The signer's regression check needs a durable, attacker-independent home, or it does not exist.** ADR-021 §Decision 2 requires this ticket to either *specify that location* or *state plainly that no tripwire exists until TKT-11*. Leaving it ambiguous is what made two drafts of the ADR wrong — do not inherit the ambiguity.
3. **Quarantine + threshold escalation are still worth building — but they bound OUR BUGS, not attackers.** A canonicalization bug or botched rotation corrupting many chains at once is the case they contain. Against a database-write adversary, fail-open is unbounded, full stop. Say so wherever this surfaces to an operator.
4. **Epoch signatures are partial.** They stop *forgery* under a retired key, not *deletion* of the epoch row. Real containment needs an externally retained rotation manifest binding every applicable ticket to its epoch head (TKT-11's domain). Implement epoch signatures, but do not claim they contain a current-key compromise.

**New coupling worth surfacing to whoever plans TKT-11:** that ticket now owns strictly more than "fiscal archive". It owns the trust domain that the ticket lifecycle trail's rollback protection, signer continuity, quarantine integrity and epoch manifests all depend on. That dependency did not exist before ADR-021 and should be on TKT-11's radar before it is planned.

<!-- sdlc:stage=backlog kind=summary -->
**Context-mémo refreshed — ADR-022 landed hours after ADR-021 and moved the ground under §Decision 9.**

Migrations no longer run at service startup ([ADR-022](../../docs/adr/ADR-022-out-of-band-service-migrations.md), TKT-66, merged #50). ADR-021 §Decision 9 said the backfill runs *"at startup, before listening, per ADR-008"*. **That premise is gone**, and I have amended the ADR rather than leave this ticket to discover it at drafting time.

**The part that is a real design problem, not a word swap:** the backfill now runs in the one-shot `access-migrate` job, and ADR-008's surviving **30-second fail-fast deadline** now bounds *that job* — which the service `depends_on` with `service_completed_successfully`. This backfill is **not DDL**: it Ed25519-signs every existing `lifecycle_events` row, so its cost scales with history. **Blow the deadline and the migrate job fails, so Access never starts.** Deciding whether it fits — or needs its own resumable job outside the migrate deadline — is this ticket's call, and it is now flagged in `readiness.uncertainties`.

**Also worth noticing:** this mémo was baked ~1 hour before it went stale. The mémo exists so the planner does not have to re-derive decision history — but a mémo is a *snapshot*, and a fast-moving registry outruns it. Re-validate `governingAdrs` against `docs/adr/` at claim time; do not trust `capturedAt` alone.

<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
Claimed by the agent (session model orchestrating; plan drafts route to gpt-5.6-sol per config.models).

Selection reason: only ticket in Ready; zero open blockers (links empty). No risk:low label, so the plan gate (Gate 2) applies.

Branch: `TKT-67-lifecycle-chain-integrity` off `origin/main` (47e7689).

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
**Plan draft — authored by `gpt-5.6-sol` (config.models.plan), via the codex companion (`task`, effort high, read-only, 15m18s).** Briefed by the orchestrator from the ticket, the context-mémo and the governing ADRs (ADR-021 as spec; ADR-002/003/008/010/012/016/020/022 as constraints), plus the six open decisions the shaping pass flagged. The drafter read the real code; it did not modify the tree.

Cross-model check: `plan` = gpt-5.6-sol, `planReview` = main-agent (this session, Opus 4.8) — distinct, invariant holds. Critique follows under `agent:plan-review`.

---

# 1. DoD

- **COS-1 — Per-ticket integrity chain**
  - Migration `0003` adds companion integrity and head tables without rewriting `lifecycle_events`.
  - `Issue`, `MarkDelivered`, and successful normal `Redeem` append the lifecycle row, integrity row, signed head, and head-change record in one transaction.
  - Existing ticket-row locking serializes each ticket. `MarkDelivered` gains the same ticket lock; no organizer-scoped lock enters any append/redemption path.
  - Verification rejects missing/reverse companion rows, sequence gaps, link/hash errors, unknown keys, bad signatures, and head mismatches.

- **COS-2 — Organizer checkpoints**
  - A background worker runs immediately and then every 60 seconds by default.
  - It checkpoints only queued head changes since the previous checkpoint, deduplicated to the latest changed head per ticket, with deterministic Merkle ordering.
  - Checkpoints are per organizer, chained, Ed25519-signed, and independently verifiable with public keys.
  - Checkpoint work never participates in ticket redemption transactions.

- **COS-3 — Signing and rotation**
  - Lifecycle keys use only the `access-lifecycle/` namespace and distinct configured seed/public material from `access-qr/`.
  - Head signatures bind domain/version, `kid`, ticket ID, ticket-local sequence, and head hash.
  - A rotation command seals all current heads with the outgoing key before rotation and retains those epoch signatures.
  - Verification validates epoch rows that exist but does not claim they are complete or attacker-resistant.

- **COS-4 — Bounded fail-open mode**
  - A corrupt-chain scan is admitted once, written to quarantine/review state, and alarms.
  - Because there is no verified predecessor, that degraded admission does not fabricate a lifecycle continuation.
  - A repeat scan of that ticket is denied and escalated.
  - Three first-time failures in 60 seconds by default flip the organizer to operator-controlled mode, defaulting to deny further corrupt-chain admissions until an operator explicitly chooses.
  - All logs, metrics, events, CLI output, and documentation label quarantine/threshold state as a software-fault bound, not adversarial containment.

- **COS-5 — Routed alarms and freshness**
  - Integrity alarms are durably published on `platform.access.lifecycle-integrity.alarm` through JetStream, backed by an Access outbox.
  - Access is not ready unless the configured operator durable consumer exists with the expected subject filter; publication backlog beyond the alarm SLO also fails readiness.
  - ERROR logs and low-cardinality OTel counters supplement, but do not replace, the durable route.
  - Checkpoint worker freshness is exposed through an OTel last-success gauge and readiness; two missed intervals make Access unready.

- **COS-6 — Verification and migration**
  - `access verify-lifecycle` loads public keys only.
  - It verifies events, integrity rows, heads, extant epoch signatures, checkpoints, checkpoint leaves, and current pending-head age.
  - Legacy history is backfilled resumably by a dedicated one-shot job after `access-migrate` and before Access starts.
  - Until backfill completes, global verification fails on incomplete coverage and the Access server remains gated off.

- **COS-7 — Gate coverage**
  - Access store smoke tests run without the current `-run TestRedeemedLifecycleMigrationPreservesHistory` allowlist.
  - `scripts/smoke.sh` verifies populated data, then proves deliberate event/integrity/head/checkpoint corruption is rejected.
  - `make check` covers pure Go tests, generated-contract drift, builds/vet, migration/backfill smoke, alarm routing, live checkpoints, and corruption detection.

# 2. Design decisions

## 1. Signer’s last-observed checkpoint root

There is no durable attacker-independent location in this repository. PostgreSQL is inside the stated adversary boundary, while NATS, LGTM, and the Access process are not durable external attestations suitable for TKT-11’s role. Therefore:

- **No freshness/rollback tripwire is claimed in TKT-67.**
- The worker keeps its last observed checkpoint `(sequence, root)` in process memory and verifies the database checkpoint chain before every extension.
- If the database head regresses relative to that live observation, or the stored chain/head is inconsistent, the worker refuses to extend it, emits a high-severity alarm, and marks checkpoint readiness unhealthy.
- A consistent truncation performed before process restart remains invisible. The new process will accept the surviving valid prefix. That is explicitly documented as TKT-11 territory.

This still refuses observable regression rather than laundering it, without pretending volatile process memory closes coordinated rollback.

## 2. Backfill placement

Use a dedicated resumable `access lifecycle-backfill` one-shot job outside `migrate()`’s 30-second deadline.

A read-only local measurement produced approximately:

- SHA-256 at 256-byte inputs: **1.95 GB/s**
- Ed25519 signing: **68,178 signatures/s**

At one million tickets, the head signatures alone cost about **14.7 seconds** of ideal CPU time. Hashing two to three million short lifecycle rows is below one second of raw crypto time, but the real job must also read and canonicalize every event and insert millions of integrity/head/change records. PostgreSQL I/O and write amplification make a 30-second guarantee indefensible even before slower production hardware is considered.

The execution model is:

1. `access-migrate` applies DDL under the existing 30-second deadline.
2. `access-lifecycle-backfill` runs without that overall deadline, using bounded per-batch/per-ticket operations and signal cancellation.
3. Access depends on both jobs completing successfully.
4. Each ticket is backfilled atomically under its ticket-row lock. Completed tickets are skipped after verification, so interruption is resumable without partial ticket chains.
5. The backfill drains its initial head-change backlog into baseline organizer checkpoints before exiting.

During backfill, `verify-lifecycle` exits non-zero because one-to-one global coverage is incomplete. That is intentional; no server is serving from the partially adopted trail.

## 3. Shared signing extraction and QR refactor

Drop both contested changes.

This ticket does create a second Ed25519 consumer inside Access, but the commonality is only the standard-library primitive and a configuration idiom. QR credentials use JWS-like encoded tokens and `access-qr/`; lifecycle signing has binary canonical forms, historical public-key verification, head/checkpoint domains, and rotation epochs. Extracting those differences behind a generic signing package would obscure security boundaries rather than consolidate meaningful behavior.

`services/access/internal/ticket/token.go` remains unchanged. Lifecycle-specific parsing and signing live in a new `internal/lifecycle` package.

## 4. Checkpoint freshness

The default interval remains **60 seconds**, but for an explicit reason:

- Once TKT-11 anchors checkpoints, it limits the permanent pre-checkpoint hole to at most roughly one minute.
- An active organizer creates at most 1,440 scheduled checkpoint opportunities per day, instead of 17,280 at five seconds.
- Five minutes would leave a materially larger irrevocable gap for little benefit, because checkpointing is delta-based and off the gate path.

This is not described as today’s fraud window.

Concrete signals:

- OTel observable gauge `access.lifecycle.checkpoint.last_success` records the Unix timestamp of the most recent completed worker pass, including no-change passes.
- `access.lifecycle.checkpoint.pending_oldest_age` records the oldest uncheckpointed head change.
- `/readyz` fails after two missed intervals, default 120 seconds.
- `verify-lifecycle` rejects a head change pending longer than `--max-pending-age`, defaulting to the configured two-interval bound.
- Smoke overrides the interval to 100 ms and asserts both checkpoint creation and exported freshness metrics.

## 5. Alarm routing

The repo currently has structured stdout/OTLP logs, OTel metrics, and durable JetStream. It has no Alertmanager, paging connector, email sender, or other proven human notification endpoint.

Use JetStream as the concrete durable routing boundary:

- Subject: `platform.access.lifecycle-integrity.alarm`
- ADR-009 envelope, schema 1.
- Payload contains only bounded identifiers and enums: alarm ID, organizer ID, ticket ID, reason, admission disposition, threshold/mode state, and occurrence time. No QR, buyer, guest reference, raw event body, or PII.
- An outbox row is committed with the quarantine/mode decision, then a worker publishes with deterministic `Nats-Msg-Id`.
- ERROR logs and OTel counters fire immediately; the durable event is the authoritative route.
- `nats-init` provisions a named durable operator inbox, and Access readiness continuously verifies that the durable exists and filters the exact subject.
- The publication SLO is five seconds; an oldest-unpublished alarm beyond that makes readiness fail and raises a separate metric.

This provides a durable, testable operator inbox, not proof that a human acknowledged a page. Production deployment must attach that durable to its paging/on-call adapter; without the configured durable, Access does not become ready in fail-open mode.

## 6. Quarantine and threshold state

State lives in the Access database:

- Per-ticket quarantine/review row.
- Per-organizer rolling failure counter and operator decision.
- Alarm outbox.

Default policy: three distinct first-time corrupt-ticket detections in 60 seconds. The scan crossing the threshold receives its one permitted fail-open admission; the organizer then enters operator-controlled mode with `deny` as the default for later corrupt tickets. Valid-chain scans remain operational. An explicit CLI lets an operator select `admit`, `deny`, or return to `normal` after remediation. A quarantined ticket’s later scans are always denied, even if the organizer is in operator-admit mode.

These controls bound canonicalization/rotation/software faults only. A database-write adversary can delete or reset all of them.

# 3. File-by-file plan

## New files

### `services/access/internal/store/migrations/0003_lifecycle_integrity.sql`

DDL sketch:

```sql
-- Companion: one row per immutable lifecycle event.
CREATE TABLE lifecycle_event_integrity (
    event_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES lifecycle_events(id),
    ticket_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(id),
    sequence bigint NOT NULL CHECK (sequence > 0),
    canonical_version smallint NOT NULL CHECK (canonical_version > 0),
    previous_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(previous_hash) = 32),
    entry_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(entry_hash) = 32),
    UNIQUE (ticket_id, sequence)
);

CREATE TABLE lifecycle_heads (
    ticket_id uuid PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES tickets(id),
    organizer_id uuid NOT NULL,
    last_sequence bigint NOT NULL CHECK (last_sequence > 0),
    canonical_version smallint NOT NULL CHECK (canonical_version > 0),
    last_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(last_hash) = 32),
    key_id text NOT NULL,
    signature bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(signature) = 64),
    changed_at timestamptz NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE lifecycle_head_epoch_signatures (
    ticket_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES tickets(id),
    key_id text NOT NULL,
    ticket_sequence bigint NOT NULL,
    canonical_version smallint NOT NULL,
    head_hash bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(head_hash) = 32),
    signature bytea NOT NULL CHECK (octet_length(signature) = 64),
    sealed_at timestamptz NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (ticket_id, key_id)
);
```

Additional tables:

- `lifecycle_head_changes`: append snapshots of signed heads; checkpoint assignment is nullable/mutable operational state.
- `lifecycle_checkpoints`: organizer-local sequence, previous root, Merkle root, leaf count, version, `kid`, signature, timestamp.
- `lifecycle_checkpoint_leaves`: ordered ticket/head snapshots used to recompute historical roots after current heads advance.
- `lifecycle_checkpoint_state`: worker cursor and current organizer checkpoint head.
- `lifecycle_integrity_quarantine`: one-time degraded admission/review record.
- `lifecycle_integrity_organizer_state`: rate window, failure count, operator-controlled mode/decision.
- `lifecycle_integrity_alarm_outbox`: sanitized alarm envelope and publication state.

Append-only triggers protect integrity rows, epoch rows, checkpoints, and checkpoint leaves. Mutable heads, queue assignment, quarantine, counters, and outbox state are explicitly documented as operational state—not cryptographic evidence against the database adversary.

Indexes are plain `CREATE INDEX`, including:

- Unique `(ticket_id, sequence)` companion coverage.
- Pending head changes by `(organizer_id, change_id)` where uncheckpointed.
- Checkpoint leaves by organizer/checkpoint/order.
- Pending alarms by creation time.
- Quarantine by organizer.

The Down migration refuses to destroy adopted integrity history. No `CONCURRENTLY`, no rewrite of `lifecycle_events`, and no index is added to that populated legacy table.

### `services/access/internal/lifecycle/canonical.go`

Pure canonicalization and crypto-domain logic:

- `CanonicalEvent`
- `HashEntry`
- `CanonicalHead`
- `CanonicalCheckpoint`
- Merkle leaf/node/root construction

Event canonical bytes bind ticket, order, organizer and slot IDs; ticket sequence; event ID/type/time; and canonical version. They expose no buyer or guest-reference parameter.

Pin:

- Lowercase RFC-4122 UUID strings.
- UTC timestamps at PostgreSQL microsecond precision.
- Legacy tie order: `occurred_at, id`.
- Explicit domain prefixes for event, head, checkpoint leaf, Merkle node, and checkpoint signature.
- Leaves sorted by raw ticket UUID bytes.
- Duplicate-last handling for an odd Merkle level.
- Empty checkpoints are not emitted.

### `services/access/internal/lifecycle/keys.go`

Lifecycle-only Ed25519 types:

- `NewSigner(seed, kid)` enforcing `access-lifecycle/`.
- `NewKeyring(raw)` accepting historical public keys only in that namespace.
- Head/checkpoint signing and public verification.
- Active-key presence validation for server/backfill modes.

It does not import or alter `internal/ticket`.

### `services/access/internal/lifecycle/canonical_test.go`

Golden byte/hash/Merkle cases and negative binding tests.

### `services/access/internal/lifecycle/keys_test.go`

Namespace separation, unknown/historical keys, public-only verification, and mutations of ticket/sequence/version/`kid`/hash.

### `services/access/internal/store/lifecycle.go`

Database implementation for:

- `appendLifecycleEvent`: inserts event + companion + signed head + head-change snapshot inside the caller’s transaction.
- `verifyTicketLifecycleTx`: one-ticket coverage/hash/head/signature verification while its ticket lock is held.
- `BackfillLifecycle`: resumable per-ticket adoption ordered by `occurred_at,id`.
- `VerifyLifecycle`: global offline verification.
- `CheckpointLifecycle`: claims committed pending changes, takes the latest per ticket, builds/stores one organizer checkpoint, and advances state without touching ticket rows.
- `SealLifecycleEpoch`: validates and signs/copies the outgoing-key head for every ticket under per-ticket locks.
- `SetLifecycleMode`: explicit operator mutation.
- Alarm outbox claim/publish-completion methods.

The verifier checks both coverage directions with joins; an integrity row whose `ticket_id` disagrees with its referenced event is an error.

### `services/access/internal/store/lifecycle_smoke_test.go`

Real-PostgreSQL tests for atomic appends, lock serialization, corrupt-chain fail-open/quarantine, threshold transition, operator decisions, alarm outbox creation, checkpoint delta behavior, and public-key verification.

### `services/access/internal/lifecyclejob/runner.go`

Two background loops:

- `CheckpointRunner`: immediate pass, interval passes, last-success tracking, stale state, metrics, and refusal on observed regression.
- `AlarmDrainer`: immediate drain, bounded retry, JetStream publication, durable-route validation, five-second backlog health, ERROR logging, and metrics.

Both accept small store/publisher/clock interfaces for deterministic tests.

### `services/access/internal/lifecyclejob/runner_test.go`

Fake-clock tests for immediate execution, missed-interval health, regression refusal, no-change heartbeat, alarm retry, route disappearance, and low-cardinality telemetry attributes.

### `services/access/cmd/access/main_test.go`

Configuration tests for:

- 60-second checkpoint default and two-interval freshness bound.
- Threshold/window defaults.
- Required `access-lifecycle/` namespace.
- Separate QR/lifecycle key material.
- Public-only verifier configuration.
- Command parsing for backfill, verification, epoch sealing, and operator mode.

### `smoke/access_lifecycle_test.go`

End-to-end alarm routing test:

- Creates/uses the operator durable.
- Corrupts a lifecycle chain in the isolated Access database.
- Scans once and observes accepted/quarantined behavior.
- Receives and validates the sanitized schema-1 alarm.
- Confirms repeat denial and escalation.
- Restores cryptographic tables and clears explicitly operational test state.

## Modified files

### `services/access/internal/store/postgres.go`

- Extend `Postgres` construction with lifecycle signer, public keyring, clock, and degraded-mode policy.
- Make `Issue` call `appendLifecycleEvent` after inserting each new ticket.
- Make `MarkDelivered` lock the ticket row before checking/appending delivery.
- In `Redeem`, retain the existing `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE`, then verify the complete ticket chain before duplicate detection.
- On a valid chain, append redemption normally.
- On an invalid chain, atomically apply quarantine/counter/mode/alarm-outbox state and return the degraded decision without appending a fake chained event.
- Extend `RedeemResult` to distinguish normal acceptance, degraded acceptance, quarantine denial, and operator-controlled denial while preserving the existing accepted/duplicate API behavior.

### `services/access/internal/store/migration_smoke_test.go`

Extend `TestRedeemedLifecycleMigrationPreservesHistory`:

1. Apply `0001`.
2. Seed issued/delivered history with deterministic timestamps, including a tie case.
3. Upgrade through `0002` and `0003`.
4. Assert legacy rows are byte-for-byte unchanged.
5. Run the resumable backfill twice.
6. Verify exactly one companion per legacy row, a correctly signed head, and queued/baseline checkpoint coverage.
7. Redeem and verify sequence 3.
8. Reassert the original immutability trigger rejects UPDATE.
9. Assert migration version 3.

### `services/access/cmd/access/main.go`

Add command dispatch:

- `lifecycle-backfill`
- `verify-lifecycle`
- `seal-lifecycle-epoch`
- `set-lifecycle-mode`

`migrate()` remains DDL-only with its existing 30-second timeout.

`verify-lifecycle` opens the database and parses only `ACCESS_LIFECYCLE_PUBLIC_KEYS`; it must not read the private-key environment variable.

Server mode:

- Loads lifecycle seed, active `kid`, historical public keys, policy, and checkpoint configuration.
- Constructs the integrity-aware `accessstore.Postgres`.
- Starts checkpoint and alarm workers.
- Splits liveness from readiness so checkpoint/alarm routing health participates only in `/readyz`.
- Stops HTTP first, then workers with a bounded shutdown, following the established Commerce worker pattern.

### `services/access/internal/api/server.go`

Map new `RedeemResult` dispositions:

- First corrupt-chain admission: HTTP 200.
- Quarantined repeat: HTTP 409, `integrity_quarantined`.
- Operator-controlled denial: HTTP 409, `integrity_operator_controlled`.
- Existing valid duplicate remains `already_redeemed`.

No cryptographic details or raw reason text are returned.

# 4. Test plan

TDD order:

1. **Canonical golden first**
   - Write failing golden tests for exact event, head, leaf/node, and checkpoint bytes.
   - Include nanosecond input truncated to microseconds, UTC conversion, lowercase UUIDs, equal timestamps ordered by event ID, canonical version/domain changes, and odd Merkle leaf count.
   - Ensure the canonical input type cannot accept `buyer_id` or `guest_order_ref`.

2. **Key and signature binding**
   - Head signature verifies with historical public keys.
   - Mutating ticket, sequence, version, `kid`, or head hash fails.
   - `access-qr/` material is rejected by lifecycle loaders.
   - Checkpoint verification uses public material only.

3. **Migration/backfill seam**
   - Extend `TestRedeemedLifecycleMigrationPreservesHistory` before changing store writes.
   - Make it fail for absent `0003`, missing backfill, non-resumability, changed timestamps, or missing signatures.

4. **Append path**
   - Implement issuance first, then delivery locking/idempotency, then redemption.
   - Concurrent delivery/redemption against one ticket must produce contiguous valid sequences in commit order.
   - Different tickets for one organizer must not wait on a shared organizer row.

5. **Fail-open policy**
   - Corrupt a signed field.
   - First scan: accepted, quarantined/reviewed, alarm owed, no fabricated lifecycle continuation.
   - Second scan: denied/escalated.
   - Three distinct corrupt tickets inside the default window: organizer changes to operator-controlled deny.
   - Operator-admit allows only first scans of other corrupt tickets; it never bypasses a ticket quarantine.
   - Comments and metric descriptions are asserted or reviewed for the non-containment label.

6. **Checkpoint worker**
   - Immediate first pass.
   - Multiple changes to one ticket collapse to the latest head in the delta.
   - A concurrent append not visible to the current checkpoint remains pending for the next pass.
   - No full `tickets`/`lifecycle_heads` scan is used; the query starts from pending `lifecycle_head_changes`.
   - Process-observed regression refuses extension and alarms.
   - Freshness becomes unhealthy after two missed intervals.

7. **Offline verifier**
   - Clean populated/backfilled database succeeds.
   - Each coverage, chain, head, epoch, Merkle, checkpoint-chain, and stale-pending case fails independently.
   - A consistent coordinated rollback fixture is documented as verifying successfully; this pins the TKT-11 limitation instead of accidentally claiming otherwise.

8. **Live smoke**
   - Populate through the existing checkout/scan flow.
   - Wait for a real checkpoint.
   - Verify lifecycle.
   - Exercise the durable alarm route.
   - Run the database corruption/restore matrix.
   - Verify clean state again.

`make check` then covers normal unit tests, `go vet -tags smoke`, generated API consistency, all Access smoke tests after the allowlist removal, the Compose backfill dependency, the live worker, telemetry, alarm route, and both positive and negative verifier runs.

# 5. Risks & pre-mortem

- **A lifecycle row is inserted without integrity.**  
  Mitigation: one append helper used by all three existing transitions, same transaction, global bidirectional coverage verification, and direct corruption tests.

- **Delivery bypasses the ticket lock.**  
  Mitigation: lock the ticket before touching delivery state or lifecycle history; concurrent delivery/redemption PostgreSQL test.

- **A head is signed without binding identity or version.**  
  Mitigation: separate head canonical form and mutation tests for every bound field.

- **Backfill bricks startup at 30 seconds.**  
  Mitigation: DDL-only migration plus a separate resumable service-gating job; no overall 30-second deadline.

- **Backfill interruption leaves a half-chain that later appears valid.**  
  Mitigation: one ticket per atomic backfill transaction; completed heads are verified before skipping; partial pre-existing coverage is treated as corruption.

- **Checkpoint delta skips a transaction because sequence allocation and commit order differ.**  
  Mitigation: consume committed pending head-change rows rather than advancing to a global sequence watermark.

- **Checkpointing accidentally serializes turnstiles.**  
  Mitigation: redemption never reads or locks checkpoint tables; the worker starts from its own change queue and writes only checkpoint state.

- **Checkpoint job silently dies.**  
  Mitigation: immediate/no-change heartbeat, last-success metric, pending-age metric, readiness deadline, verifier age bound, and smoke assertion.

- **A checkpoint is unrecomputable after a ticket advances.**  
  Mitigation: persist signed head snapshots as checkpoint leaves instead of trying to reconstruct historical leaves from current heads.

- **Fail-open appends onto a corrupt predecessor and creates misleading evidence.**  
  Mitigation: degraded admission is recorded only in explicitly non-cryptographic quarantine/review state; the broken immutable chain is left untouched.

- **Alarm publication is lost after admission.**  
  Mitigation: alarm outbox committed with quarantine/mode state, immediate drainer, deterministic JetStream ID, retry, five-second readiness SLO, durable route verification.

- **A log/metric is mistaken for paging.**  
  Mitigation: JetStream durable is the required route; logs/metrics are secondary. Documentation states that human acknowledgement remains deployment/on-call responsibility.

- **Epoch signatures are presented as current-key containment.**  
  Mitigation: verifier checks only extant rows, never completeness; rotation docs and operator output repeat that deletion/current-key rewrite remain possible until TKT-11.

- **Canonicalization drifts with PostgreSQL timestamp precision.**  
  Mitigation: normalize to UTC microseconds before signing and pin exact bytes in golden and migration tests.

- **The new Access smoke tests never run.**  
  Mitigation: remove the package’s `-run` allowlist.

# 6. Out of scope

- TKT-11’s external attestation/trust domain.
- A durable attacker-independent last-observed checkpoint root.
- Detection of targeted ticket/checkpoint rollback, consistent prefix truncation, whole-organizer deletion, or database snapshot restore.
- External epoch completeness manifests.
- Containment of a compromised current lifecycle private key.
- Attacker-independent quarantine, counters, or operator mode.
- A claim that fail-open bounds a database-write adversary.
- Fiscal archive, NF525 certification, or coordinated money/ticket anchors.
- ADR-016/TKT-11 rollback closure.
- New ticket lifecycle event types, transfers, resale, reissue, pass entry/exit, or ticket-local compression checkpoints.
- Organizer-wide lifecycle ordering or global ticket-set completeness.
- A shared Access signing package.
- Any refactor of `internal/ticket/token.go`.
- QR key rotation changes.
- A new deployment system or built-in third-party paging adapter; TKT-67 provides and gates the durable in-repo alarm route, while production on-call integration remains deployment configuration.

## 1. Critique — accept / amend / reject

### ACCEPTED as drafted

- **Decision 1 — no freshness tripwire is claimed.** Correct, and it is the choice ADR-021 §D2
  demands be made explicitly rather than left ambiguous. The draft picks "state plainly that no
  tripwire exists until TKT-11" *and* still refuses observable regression from process memory,
  while naming that volatile memory closes nothing across a restart. That is the honest reading.
- **Decision 3 — both contested items dropped.** `internal/signing` extraction and the
  `token.go` refactor are refused, with the right reason: the commonality is `crypto/ed25519` and
  a config idiom, not behaviour. QR is JWS-ish text tokens; lifecycle is binary canonical forms
  with historical verification and rotation epochs. A shared package would hide the security
  boundary, not consolidate it. `token.go` stays byte-for-byte untouched.
- **Decision 2 — backfill leaves the migrate job.** `access-migrate` stays DDL-only under its 30s
  deadline; a separate resumable `access-lifecycle-backfill` job runs without an overall deadline
  and Access depends on both. The arithmetic checks out (1M ÷ 68,178 sig/s ≈ 14.7s of *ideal* CPU
  for head signatures alone, before read, canonicalize, and millions of row inserts) — a 30s
  guarantee is indefensible. This is the call ADR-021 §D9's amendment asked for.
- **Per-ticket atomic backfill under the ticket lock, resumable, skip-after-verify.** Correct, and
  it is what makes interruption safe.
- **Degraded admission does not append to the chain.** Right call, and worth stating why: appending
  onto an unverified predecessor would chain from a bad `previous_hash` and permanently poison the
  ticket's chain, converting a detectable one-row corruption into an unrecoverable one.
- **ADR-009 envelope, schema 1, bounded identifiers only.** Verified: ADR-009 §5 owns the envelope
  (`{id,type,occurred_at,schema,data}`), and the payload carries no PII/`guest_order_ref` per
  ADR-003 §D3. A brand-new event type at schema 1 bumps nothing (ADR-017 unaffected).
- **API compatibility.** Verified: `ScanRejected.reason` is already `{type: string}` free-form
  (`services/access/api/openapi.yaml:53`), so the two new 409 reasons need no schema break.
- **Merkle root, delta, sorted leaves.** ADR-021 §D2 mandates the Merkle root; not re-litigated.

### AMENDED — the draft is wrong or incomplete here

**A1 (blocking) — readiness gating takes the turnstile down over scaffolding. The draft's own
mitigation is illusory.**
The draft says it "splits liveness from readiness so checkpoint/alarm routing health participates
only in `/readyz`", treating `/readyz` as the safe place to put it. **It is not.** The container
healthcheck is `test: ["CMD", "/app", "healthcheck"]` (`compose.yaml:50`), and `healthcheck()`
probes `http://localhost:<port>/readyz` (`cmd/access/main.go:75`). So `/readyz` **is** the health
gate: unready → unhealthy → `depends_on: service_healthy` blocks dependents and `compose up --wait`
(which `scripts/smoke.sh:47` runs) fails.

That makes the draft's COS-5 propose three new ways to take the scan path down:
1. the operator durable not existing,
2. alarm publication backlog > 5s,
3. checkpoint stale for two intervals.

Each contradicts ADR-021 §D6's whole basis — *"The trail's job is to make tampering evident, not to
make the door brittle"* — and §D6 chose fail-open **precisely** so our own bugs never deny real
customers. Failing readiness on a NATS blip denies every customer at the gate, which is strictly
worse than the fail-open case the ADR accepted. Worse, the checkpoint is by the ADR's own account
(§D2, §Consequences) **scaffolding that buys no detection today** — gating the door on stale
scaffolding is the most disproportionate version of this.

The smoke config makes it concrete: the draft sets the interval to **100 ms** in smoke with a
two-interval readiness bound = **200 ms**. Any GC pause or DB hiccup over 200 ms flips Access
unhealthy and fails the gate. That is a flaky-gate generator.

**Amendment:**
- **Durable route: validate at *startup*, fail-fast.** If the configured durable is absent or
  filters the wrong subject, Access **refuses to boot**. This satisfies §D6's "an unmonitored
  deployment must not run this scheme in fail-open" *better* than a readiness probe — a
  misconfigured deployment never starts, and a live one is not hostage to a broker blip.
- **Alarm backlog and checkpoint freshness: metric + alarm, never readiness.** ADR-021
  §Consequences says freshness must be **monitored**, not gated. Keep
  `access.lifecycle.checkpoint.last_success` and `…pending_oldest_age`; drop both from `/readyz`.
- `verify-lifecycle` keeps its `--max-pending-age` check — that is the right place for it, because
  the verifier is an audit tool, not the door.

**A2 (blocking) — `MarkDelivered`'s existing idempotency will break the append.**
`MarkDelivered` currently inserts with `ON CONFLICT(ticket_id,event_type) DO NOTHING`
(`postgres.go:130`), so a redelivery is a silent no-op. The event id is deterministic
(`uuid.NewSHA1(...":delivered")`, `postgres.go:129`), and the draft's integrity table is
`PRIMARY KEY (event_id)` — so a blind `appendLifecycleEvent` on a repeat call inserts no lifecycle
row but *does* attempt an integrity row, hitting a PK conflict and turning today's silent-success
redelivery into a hard error. The draft's "lock the ticket row before checking/appending" gestures
at this but never states it.
**Amendment:** the append helper is called **only when the lifecycle insert actually inserted**
(rows-affected under the ticket lock). Idempotency is resolved *before* the append, never by it.
A test for the repeat `MarkDelivered` call is required, asserting: still succeeds, no second
integrity row, sequence unchanged.

**A3 — drop two of the eight tables; they are derivable, and two sources of truth diverge.**
- `lifecycle_checkpoint_leaves` duplicates `lifecycle_head_changes`. The draft already stores
  signed head *snapshots* in `head_changes` with a checkpoint assignment, so checkpoint N's leaf
  set is exactly `SELECT DISTINCT ON (ticket_id) … WHERE checkpoint_id = N ORDER BY ticket_id,
  change_id DESC`. The stated justification ("unrecomputable after a ticket advances") is already
  answered by the snapshot. Tampering with the assignment changes the recomputed root, which the
  signature catches — the same protection the leaves table would have.
- `lifecycle_checkpoint_state` is fully derivable: the worker cursor is
  `head_changes WHERE checkpoint_id IS NULL`; the organizer's current checkpoint head is
  `MAX(sequence)` on `lifecycle_checkpoints`.

Eight tables → six, one less index, and a whole class of "the cache disagrees with the truth" bugs
removed. The `DISTINCT ON` ordering gets pinned by a golden test like every other canonical choice.

**A4 — the in-process regression check must be O(1), not a full chain walk.**
"Verifies the database checkpoint chain before every extension" grows unboundedly for a long-lived
organizer, every 60s, forever. The worker only needs: the stored latest checkpoint matches the
`(sequence, root)` it remembers, and the new checkpoint links to it. Full-chain verification is
`verify-lifecycle`'s job.

**A5 — pin the Merkle duplicate-last hazard with a comment, not just a golden test.**
"Duplicate-last handling for an odd level" is the CVE-2012-2459 shape: with duplication, two leaf
multisets can yield one root. It is **not reachable here** because leaves are deduplicated to one
per ticket and sorted by raw ticket UUID — but that safety is a consequence of the dedup, not of
the tree. A future reader relaxing the dedup would silently introduce root ambiguity. One comment
at the duplication site naming the dependency; the dedup itself gets an explicit test.

**A6 — the degraded admission's only record is mutable operational state.**
Given A-accepted "no fabricated continuation", a corrupt-chain admission writes nothing to
`lifecycle_events`, so the *fact that a person physically walked in* survives only in the
quarantine row, which the draft classes as mutable operational state. Against the adversary that is
irrelevant (they already won). But for the case these controls actually bound — **our own bug**, a
canonicalization drift admitting many tickets — we would want to reconstruct exactly who was
admitted during the degraded window, after remediation. Give the quarantine table the same
append-only trigger the repo already uses (`lifecycle_events_immutable`, `0001_tickets.sql`) for
its admission records, keeping only the operator-decision fields mutable. Cheap (one existing
pattern), and it is the difference between reconstructing a bug's blast radius and guessing at it.
Still labelled non-adversarial everywhere.

### REJECTED

- Nothing in the draft is rejected outright. A1 is the only place it is actually *wrong* (as
  opposed to incomplete), and it is wrong on a verified fact about this repo rather than on judgement.

### Per-finding verdicts — verified against HEAD, not the base branch

| # | Verdict | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** — checkpoint signs unauthenticated head snapshots | **CONFIRMED — and worse than reported** | Fixed |
| **R2** — stored canonical versions never verified | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed |
| **R3** — dead-lettered alarms vanish from the backlog metric | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed |
| **R4** — failed passes refresh `last_success` | **CONFIRMED** | Fixed |

**R1, and the part the review understated.** It said a database *writer* could inject a snapshot. It
is worse: `lifecycle_head_changes_immutable` fires `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` **only** — INSERT was
never covered, and an append-only queue must accept inserts. So **no DDL privilege was needed at
all**; a plain INSERT of a fabricated newer snapshot for a real ticket would win the dedup, and the
verifier — recomputing the root from the very same rows — would agree with the forgery. Signer and
verifier concurring on attacker-supplied input is not verification.

Why it is critical despite the checkpoint detecting nothing today: the checkpoint's **only** purpose
is to be the structure TKT-11 anchors (§D2). A root over invented heads is worse than no anchor.

Fix: the snapshot now carries the head's own Ed25519 signature; the worker verifies it before signing
a root, and the verifier verifies it before a leaf counts. Both also join `tickets` to confirm
ownership — the head signature binds ticket/sequence/version/kid but **not** the organizer, so
nothing else stopped a change being filed under another organizer's checkpoint. **Scoped honestly:
this closes fabrication, not replay.** An older genuine snapshot can still be re-queued; that is the
rollback class §Threat model already records as undetected.

**R2.** `canonical_version` sat on five tables and was read by nothing. The version does travel inside
the signed domain prefix (`…/v1`), so the hash always covered it — the loose column was a second copy
nothing enforced, and it is the discriminator future migrations dispatch on. Now verified everywhere,
rejecting anything but v1. Same shape as ADR-017 §5b′: dispatch on the version before trusting bytes.

**R3.** Correct and nasty: the backlog gauge fell to **zero at the exact moment** an alarm became
permanently undeliverable — the unmonitored-deployment case §D6 forbids, arriving silently. Dead
letters now have their own gauge; non-zero means fail-open is running unwatched.

**R4.** Correct. Fixed by not counting a pass in which any organizer failed.

### R1 — you are right, and it is the fourth instance of ADR-021's signature failure

I wrote "Refuse to boot unmonitored" over a check that proves an inbox **exists**. Nothing in the
repo consumes that durable, so the default stack passes and is unmonitored — and `docs/development.md`
already said "attaching that durable to a pager is the deployment's job", contradicting the claim two
paragraphs away. You caught my own docs disagreeing with my own code.

I took your second option, because the first is not achievable: **no boot-time check can prove a human
will act on a page.** So:
- `RequireAlarmRoute` now documents exactly what it buys — retention, not monitoring.
- **ADR-021 §D6 is amended**: TKT-67 delivered routing and retention; *monitoring is a deployment
  obligation this code cannot discharge*. §Status records this as the **fourth** time the ADR has
  described a control by its intent rather than its reach — the three in §The trust boundary, plus
  this one.
- Added `access.lifecycle.alarm.durable_pending`: a durable nobody drains accumulates. That is the
  closest observable proxy for the forbidden unmonitored deployment, and the docs now say to alert on it.

### R3 — accepted on the race, **partially declined on the remedy**, with reasons

The **mode-overwrite race is a real bug** and is fixed properly: the flip is now conditional on
`mode='normal'` in one atomic statement, so the system may only move an organizer *out* of normal and
can never take a human's `operator_admit` back.

I **did not** serialize the degraded path on an organizer row. The scenario this protection exists for
is a canonicalization bug corrupting every chain at doors-open — where **every** scan takes the
degraded path and would queue behind that one row. That is exactly the organizer-wide contention
ADR-021 §Option 1 rejected the money journal for, reintroduced at the worst possible moment. §D6's
purpose is to escalate to a human, not to cap admissions precisely — it already concedes fail-open is
unbounded against an adversary.

So the threshold is **approximate under concurrency and converges**: a simultaneous batch may not flip,
the next scan does. That is now documented at the call site and tested concurrently
(`TestConcurrentCorruptScansConvergeOnOperatorControl`), including the invariant that matters under any
concurrency — **no ticket is ever admitted twice**. If you want exactness at that cost, say so and
I'll take the lock.

### R4 — and the reason it mattered more than it looked

Fixed as specified: the real sequence-1 head bytes are captured before redemption and restored. Nothing
in that test touches `cfg.Signer` now.

### On method — the part worth recording

Your R2 fix was initially **unverified by me**. I mutation-checked it (neutralize the fix, keep it
compiling, expect failure) and *no test failed* — I had fixed the code and written no test that could
catch its absence. The tests I then added fail with
`Accepted:true Decision:accepted` for a reassigned integrity row, which is the vulnerability stated
out loud. R3's fix was mutation-checked the same way and did fail correctly.

That is the second time this round that running the check beat assuming it. Both R1 and R2 were
overclaims of mine that survived my own reading.

governingAdrs.rule: THE spec for this ticket. Deliberate divergences from the money journal (Ed25519 not HMAC; sign the head not every entry; per-ticket not per-organizer) must NOT be 'fixed' back. §The trust boundary governs every claim.
§D7 — coordinated rollback is deferred to TKT-11. Do not claim to close it; do not re-solve it here.
§D2 trace-derived redemption (why this matters); §D3 no PII and no guest_order_ref in the canonical form; §D4's NF525 no-schema-change constraint is money-specific and does NOT bind this trail.
One DB per service. Chain, heads, checkpoints, signing, verification all live inside Access. Link to orders/journal by identifier only — no cross-DB FK, no shared chain.
Access already owns Ed25519 QR signing with an injected seed + kid (token.go:61-78, the access-qr/ namespace convention). Reuse the idiom, separate the key material.
Contention model: lock the ticket, never the organizer. The reason ADR-021 rejected the money journal's granularity.

SUPERSEDES ADR-008 ON PLACEMENT. Migrations run OUT-OF-BAND as a one-shot `<service>-migrate` Compose job (`migrate` subcommand); the server path never migrates and the service `depends_on` the job with `service_completed_successfully`. There is no 'before listening' any more. Single-invoker serialization is the invariant — advisory locking is deliberately deferred, and anything that could launch two migrate jobs per service must adopt it first.

SUPERSEDED ON PLACEMENT by ADR-022 — do NOT read it as 'migrations run at startup'. What still stands and still binds: goose v3 as a library, migrations embedded via embed.FS, per-service schema ownership, seed data as ordinary migrations, and FAIL-FAST UNDER A 30-SECOND DEADLINE.

Plain CREATE INDEX, never CONCURRENTLY — still. ADR-022 satisfied precondition (1) (migrations left startup), but the preconditions are CONJUNCTIVE and (2)/(3) remain false, so the decision is unchanged.
